content.comment_body: On my laptop with Windows 10, I connected a USB-to-serial adapter and the computer installed the drivers, assigning it to COM3. When I run the application that should use COM3, I receive an error saying it's unable to access the IP address for COM3. I'm unsure how to fix this. Thank you.

Did you confirm your setup? You mentioned the USB adapter installed as COM3 and you tried connecting on COM3, but your screenshot shows COM4. Which COM port is actually correct? Which [product_name] are you using? What hardware type did you select in the configuration?
Thanks for your response. I made a mistake, it should have been COM4. The issue was resolved by setting the correct hardware type in the configuration.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered issues connecting to a [product_name] device via USB-to-serial adapter on Windows 10 due to an incorrect hardware type setting. The connectivity error was not related to drivers or actual physical connection, but rather an application configuration issue. Adjusting the hardware setting in the program resolved the problem.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates easy hardware connection and expects the software to either automatically detect or clearly guide hardware selection when using widely available USB adapters on current operating systems.
